# **1\. Executive Summary**

## **\-Primary Value Propositions:**

* You could generate quotes as you estimate instead of estimating and then generating a quote. This simplifies the estimating-quote building process from something that could be an hour-plus long with multiple steps to something more streamlined that could be done in 10-15 minutes at most  
* Modernizing the estimating and quote building workflow with better UI and AI.: Let's just say you put in the scope of work and boom it gives you a V1 quote you could conversation with the AI based off the context in that "for example you could be like all right now add a 9% sales tax instead of 10 or let's add 5% discount to these following line items ABC. And boom it will update and provide a new version of that quote. The goal is that the user could chat in natural language. and as they're typing in submitting, they'll see on the right hand side, what their quote is gonna look like. It should use LLM's to par the inputs.  
* Easily upload new products and keep track of your price book to understand margins of each product you sell. These margins will be shown once the quote is generated. For example, this is what it's going to cost to do the project, and this is how much you're projected to make based off of the quote and the margins built into your product price book.  
* Easily download, share, and keep track of all the quotes that you are generating with AI inside of your different projects.

# **2\. Scope definition**

 

## **\-In Scope:** 

* Sidebar that gives you access to all your projects. Once you click on a project, it will pull up the chat history, workspace, and log for that specific project.  
* A search tab allows you to filter and search through all your different projects based off just typing in the project name or specific details about the project. (Housed within side bar)  
* A price book tab that allows you to: add new products, search existing products, upload CSV files of product catalogs. This will be used when building your quotes and asking for certain material, line items, and all that. (Housed within side bar)  
* Default home screen where you type in the name to create a new project and select what services and products are going to be used within the project. Then When you hit submit, it will automatically Add that new project to the projects section And open up a new project chat.  
* A project chat window that is similar to a ChatGPT   And when a project is first created, it will ask you to enter your scope of work. There will be three key sections within this chat window, which will look like how Cursor Terminal is set up. Part one is the chat window where you are prompting your quote based off of the scope of work. Part two is a workspace section where you can upload your work docs and images that will be used to quote and build your estimate. Part three is a quote log section that will house all of the versions of your quote that you push to production Where you could then go back and access to either download or revise.    
* A PDF downloadable quote that lists things like: Product number, Product name, List price, Discount to customer, Quantity, Total price, Taxes, Shipping and handling, Final price of the project. In this PDF, the company could add their logo to it will have their address as well. But this is what gets created when they finish up a quote and this side is good.   
* Login and sign-in credentials for people to be able to create an account to access features and services of the platform. A company will be able to add licenses to their account; Which means teams or multiple team members could collaborate within the company account.  
* Pricing page so that Users can purchase from website, with credit or debit card or PayPal, so I have to be able to collect those payment  via something like Stripe.   
* Onboarding new users once purchased, so they could create an account and be on boarded to the platform.  
* Front-end landing page style website with information about the software and our services and problems we're solving along with pricing. It just serves as a front-facing website where if a user decides to move forward, they could purchase a seat. For those who have already purchased a seat, they could log in to their account.

## **\-Out of Scope:** 

* App version of this SaaS platform.  
* Dashboard with analytics and data when it comes to things like: Quotes created, Quotes  sent out, Quotes approved, Date filters, Revenue Filters, etc.  
* Being able to create full proposals where clients could sign, date, and accept formal proposals.  
* Building out different pages like a services page, product features, blog section for that front-end website.  
* **Integration:**  Quote/Estimates sync with CRM, project management, or accounting systems (e.g., Salesforce, PandaDoc, QuickBooks). 

# **3\. Target market and user analysis**

## **\-Total Addressable Market (TAM)**

* A blue-Collar Industry brick and mortar service-based business doing between $2M+ in annual revenue:  general contractors, electricians, plumbers, HVAC companies, roofers, painters, flooring installers, drywall and stucco contractors, masonry and concrete specialists, tile and stone installers, handymen, carpentry shops, fencing contractors, pool builders, asphalt or paving companies, landscaping companies,  security system installers, garage door companies,  low-voltage and structured cabling companies, telecommunications installers, internet and fiber contractors, alarm monitoring providers, audio-visual and home theater installers, fire alarm.  
* 500k \+ companies and 3 million \+ employees

## **\-Technology Profile**

* They probably use tools like ServiceTitan, QuickBooks, Jobber, CompanyCam, System Surveyor, and have some kind of project management and CRM tool.

## **\-Pain Points**

1\. Data & Information Gathering Pain Points

* **Scattered project data:** Material lists, labor rates, and past project details live in emails, PDFs, and spreadsheets instead of a centralized system.

* **No version control:** Estimators constantly overwrite old versions or lose track of the latest file revisions.

* **Manual takeoffs:** Engineers waste hours counting symbols and devices on drawings instead of using AI-powered detection or import tools.

* **Difficulty reusing past work:** No quick way to reference prior jobs, pricing, or templates, leading to repetitive rebuilding of similar estimates.  
   

2\. Time & Workflow Efficiency Pain Points

* **Estimates take too long:** What could be automated in seconds often takes hours or days of manual entry and formatting.

* **Repetitive tasks:** Copy-pasting line items, re-calculating margins, or re-formatting proposals consumes valuable time.

* **No automation:** Labor hours, markups, or tax calculations all require manual math and double-checking.

* **Administrative bottlenecks:** Engineers and coordinators spend more time building documents than actually engineering or managing projects.

* **Missed bid deadlines:** When multiple RFPs hit at once, manual quoting makes it impossible to submit all bids on time. 

3\. Accuracy & Cost Control Pain Points

* **Human error:** Manual entry leads to typos, wrong quantities, or missing line items that can cost thousands.

* **Inconsistent pricing:** Each estimator uses their own spreadsheet formulas, so margins and rates vary by person.

* **Untracked revisions:** When pricing changes mid-project, there’s no clear record of who adjusted what and why.

* **Difficulty managing change orders:** Adjusting an existing quote or adding new scope requires rebuilding sections manually.

* **No validation:** There’s no built-in check to flag missing parts, mismatched units, or unrealistic labor estimates.  
* **Difficult client communication:** Making quick revisions for a client’s request means digging through old documents and re-exporting everything.   
  5\. Knowledge Management Pain Points  
* **No institutional memory:** When a senior estimator leaves, all pricing logic and experience leave with them.

* **Tribal knowledge problem:** Key assumptions live in someone’s head instead of a centralized, searchable database.

* **Hard to train new estimators:** New hires struggle to learn inconsistent or undocumented workflows.  
   

6\. Customer Experience & Professionalism Pain Points

* **Slow turnaround times:** Clients expect same-day or next-day proposals, but manual methods can take several days.

* **Inflexibility:** Making scope changes or offering optional alternates requires a complete rework.

* **Lost opportunities:** When quotes take too long or contain errors, customers go with faster competitors.

7\. Business Operations & Growth Pain Points

* **Inability to scale:** Manual workflows can’t keep up as quote volume grows.

* **No integration:** Estimates don’t sync with CRM, project management, or accounting systems (e.g., Salesforce, PandaDoc, QuickBooks).

* **Poor forecasting:** Leadership lacks visibility into pipeline value or estimated backlog.

* **Reactive pricing:** No insights into profitability until after projects are complete.

* **Limited bandwidth:** Engineers get bogged down in admin work instead of high-value design or oversight tasks.

8\. Competitive Disadvantage Pain Points

* **Slower response time than AI-enabled competitors:** Losing bids because others can quote faster with automated tools.

* **Higher labor cost:** Manual estimating eats up billable engineering hours.  
     
* **No adaptive intelligence:** Traditional tools can’t learn from past wins/losses to refine pricing strategies.

## **\-Success Criteria:**

1\. Estimators, Engineers & Preconstruction Roles

These are your *power users* — the ones who live inside the tool daily.

**Primary Success Criteria:**

* **Quote speed improvement:** Can they build a complete, accurate quote **50–80% faster** than before (e.g., minutes instead of hours)?

* **Takeoff automation accuracy:** Does AI correctly detect 90%+ of symbols, devices, and materials on drawings or plans?

* **Template and data reuse:** Can they quickly duplicate past projects, apply saved templates, and auto-update materials and pricing?

* **Error reduction:** Fewer manual calculation mistakes or double entries compared to Excel-based workflows.

* **Ease of revision:** Can they instantly adjust line items, margins, or scope changes without rebuilding the entire estimate?

* **Export & presentation quality:** Do proposal outputs look clean, branded, and professional without manual formatting?

* **Confidence in AI suggestions:** AI recommendations (pricing, labor hours, part substitutions) must be explainable and editable, not “black box.”

**What success feels like to them:**  
 They finish bids early, trust their numbers, and no longer dread repetitive takeoffs or formatting — their work output doubles without burnout.

---

🏗️ 2\. Project Managers & Coordinators

They depend on the **clarity and traceability** of quotes to manage execution.

**Primary Success Criteria:**

* **Clean handoffs:** Estimates seamlessly convert into scopes, budgets, or bills of materials for field execution.

* **Change order agility:** Updating a quote for revised scope takes minutes, not hours.

* **Centralized version control:** Everyone works off the same document, with a full audit trail of changes.

* **Cross-team visibility:** PMs can instantly view status of pending, approved, or lost quotes.

* **Integration with project systems:** Quotes sync automatically with Procore, Monday, Smartsheet, or Salesforce.

* **Communication clarity:** AI-generated summaries make it easy to share client-facing or internal updates.

**What success feels like to them:**  
 No lost revisions, no confusion about latest numbers, and zero surprises between estimating and field operations.

---

💼 3\. Operations Leaders & Executives (Decision-Makers)

These are the **economic buyers** — they care about scalability, margins, and predictability.

**Primary Success Criteria:**

* **Bid-to-win ratio increase:** AI insights help prioritize and tailor bids, improving win rates by 10–30%.

* **Standardization:** All quotes use consistent cost structures, markups, and presentation templates across teams.

* **Profit margin visibility:** Real-time dashboards show projected gross margin per job before sending quotes.

* **Labor efficiency:** Fewer estimators handle more bids (2–3× throughput) without additional headcount.

* **Forecast accuracy:** AI data feeds improve pipeline predictability and revenue projections.

* **Reduced rework:** Minimal revisions from clients due to clearer proposals.

* **Faster sales cycles:** Shorter time from RFP to signed proposal (measurable in days saved).

**What success feels like to them:**  
 They can scale quote volume, tighten margins, and trust forecasting without hiring more people or micromanaging the team.

---

🤝 4\. Sales & Account Executives

These users rely on quotes as **sales tools**, not just technical documents.

**Primary Success Criteria:**

* **Speed to proposal:** Ability to create a client-ready proposal same-day after a discovery call.

* **Quote flexibility:** Easy to add options, alternates, or “good / better / best” packages.

* **Visual presentation:** Branded proposals that impress clients and clearly communicate value.

* **Live pricing confidence:** Always-accurate cost data for instant quoting on calls.

* **CRM sync:** Quotes auto-attach to deals in Salesforce, HubSpot, or GHL.

* **Follow-up automation:** AI reminders for when a quote is viewed or needs revisiting.

**What success feels like to them:**  
 They close faster, follow up smarter, and never lose a deal because the proposal took too long.

---

📊 5\. Finance, Admin, and IT Stakeholders

They care about **data integrity, compliance, and integration** across the tech stack.

**Primary Success Criteria:**

* **Accurate cost coding:** Estimates align with accounting categories for smooth billing.

* **Automated data flow:** No double entry between estimating and QuickBooks/ERP.

* **Approval control:** Multi-level approvals for discounts or margin changes.

* **Audit trail:** Traceability for every quote version and approval step.

* **System reliability & security:** Cloud-based, backed up, and compliant with IT standards.

🔌 7\. Industry-Specific Success Criteria

**Low-Voltage / Security Integrators:**

* Automatically map devices from drawings (cameras, access points, panels).

* Generate wiring diagrams, cable lengths, and cost breakdowns instantly.

* Deliver branded proposals with camera layouts, specs, and warranty details.

**HVAC / Electrical / Plumbing:**

* Accurately calculate labor hours, materials, and unit pricing from standard assemblies.

* Adjust costs dynamically for regional labor rates or supplier updates.

* Link estimates directly to service maintenance contracts.

**General Contractors:**

* Aggregate and standardize subcontractor bids using AI normalization.

* Automatically compare vendor quotes and detect outliers.

* Roll up project summaries for executive approval.

# **5\. Technical Architecture & Stack**

**Backend:** Supabase (Database, Auth, Storage, Events)

**Payments:** Stripe

## **7\. AI Context & Guardrails Layer**

### **🎯 Goal: Prevent hallucinations and maintain quote integrity tied to Price Book \+ Project context.**

#### **A. Intelligence Modes (Toggle per Project)**

1. **Strict (RAG‑Only):** Only use retrieved items from Price Book/project files.  
2. **Hybrid (RAG‑First):** Use retrieved items; allow generative suggestions if user approves. 

#### **B. Clarifying‑Question Templates**

* “Which brand or equivalent?” \[Brand A\] \[Brand B\] \[No preference\]  
* “How many cameras per floor?”  
* “Include labor?” \[Yes/No/Separate line\]

#### **C. Safe Fallback – Draft Quote Preview**

* Display non‑committable draft with missing fields highlighted.  
* Commit to Log once validated.

#### **D. AI Context Memory**

* Persist frequently used product families, markup rules, and templates per user.  
* Recall project‑specific preferences (e.g., tax %, default materials).

#### **E. Auth & Analytics**

* Supabase Auth for user \+ license management.  
* Supabase Events for quote metrics and system telemetry.

#### **F. AI Integration Details**

* Provider: OpenAI GPT‑5  
* Prompt management: LangChain / Vercel AI SDK  
* Vector retrieval: pgvector (Supabase)  
* Deterministic math enforcement (tax %, discounts, margins auditable in Quote Log)
